_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS R1252's CONTRACT IS NOT VACUOUS — run it from the
repository root:
cargo run -q --manifest-path tools/injection-harness/Cargo.toml -- \
crates/mnemosyne-server/sweeps/schema-compiler.sweep.json
WHAT THE CONTRACT IS. The descriptor set this crate embeds and serves is one
a CRATE compiled, in the build script's own process, and not one a program
did. Six jobs of this repository's workflow used to install `protobuf-compiler`
from the Ubuntu archive because `tonic-build` shells out to `protoc`; on
2026-08-19 four consecutive runs of `main` died at that step, the last of
them after R1251 had already given apt retries and a shorter timeout.
THE LAW IS ASSERTED AGAINST THE REAL BUILD, so every injection here edits
the build script rather than a fixture. The three are the three ways the
claim can stop being true: the compiler is a program again, the compiler is
asked for something else, and the file is compiled under another name.
ONE OF THEM NEEDS `protoc` ON THE MACHINE RUNNING THE SWEEP, and that is
the point rather than an oversight: proving that the protoc route is caught
means taking it. On a machine without the binary that injection does not go
red, it fails to BUILD — which the harness reports as a discrepancy rather
than as a pass, so the sweep refuses instead of lying. Nothing else in this
repository needs the binary any more, this file included.

injections.name: the-schema-compiler-goes-back-to-being-a-program
injections.why: the state this crate was in until R1252, and the one that put a network fetch in front of six jobs. `compile_protos` spawns a `protoc` binary; its descriptor agrees with `protox`'s byte for byte once `source_code_info` is set aside and carries the same 264 locations as a set, but in a different ORDER — which is what makes the embedded bytes say which compiler produced them

injections.name: the-compiler-is-asked-for-something-else
injections.why: the drift that costs the generated Rust its doc comments and leaves everything else looking right. `include_source_info` is what carries the schema's comments through; a build script that stops asking for it produces a smaller descriptor that still serves every reflection client correctly, so nothing but a comparison notices

injections.name: the-file-is-compiled-under-another-name
injections.why: the one that changes what every reflection client asks for the file BY. A descriptor records the include-relative path, so opening the schema by its path from the crate root renames it to `proto/mnemosyne.proto` — a rename of the crate's published schema, made by moving an argument
